html:
SMTO-SKL-0040 — Google Drive didn't allow this action

GUID: 0d8acea9-3482-5587-bb6e-57b6c66dea5b
Slug: google-drive-permission-denied
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Google Drive refused this action for your account. Usually the account can view the file but not change, copy or download it, or the owner or your organization has restricted it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file in Google Drive with the same account and check whether you are a viewer, commenter or editor. Viewers and commenters can't change files, and owners can block downloading or copying.
  2. If you need more access, ask the file's owner to share it with you as an editor. Only the owner or an editor can raise your access.
  3. If you have another Google account with access, tell SMTO to use that account instead. The action works only with an account Google allows to do it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the action and the file in Google Drive reflects it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Google administrator. Don't ask the owner to make the file public just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned HTTP 403 without a recognized scope, shared-drive membership or export-size reason (provider_error permission_denied).

What this means

  • Drive receives HTTP 403 without a recognized scope, shared-drive membership or export-size reason. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Drive receives HTTP 403 without a recognized scope, shared-drive membership or export-size reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect file permissions, account and safe provider reason rather than automatically reauthorizing.

How to fix it

  • A 403 with no allowlisted reason maps to permission_denied. Check the file's sharing role for the selected account (google_drive.permissions), owner restrictions on download/copy, and Workspace admin policies; switch to an account that has the required role rather than retrying.
  • Review provider file permissions and the selected account.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review provider file permissions and the selected account.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual provider access requirement is satisfied for the intended operation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
